title: Agent Autonomy Level Assigner
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Evaluation activity in which learners recommend an autonomy level from 0 (Suggest only) to 3 (Act and report) for each of eight illustrative research tasks, using three given attributes: whether the task is reversible, whether its result leaves the researcher's control, and whether it can be verified quickly. Each task gets one attempt in a fixed order, followed by the correct level, the reason, and the assignment rule that applied. The run ends with a score out of 8, a mastery statement at 7 of 8, and how many tasks fell at each level.

educational.topic: Setting agent autonomy from the properties of a research task
learningObjectives: Recommend an autonomy level from 0 to 3 for each of eight research tasks from its reversibility, reach, and verifiability, with at least 7 of 8 correct
prerequisites: Agent autonomy, reversibility, reach, and verifiability
The four autonomy levels: Suggest only, Approve each step, Act within a boundary, and Act and report

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons reachable with the Tab key and activated with Enter or Space; the level buttons carry aria-label and aria-pressed; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check or X symbols as well as a blue or orange outline; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Level 0 / Level 1 / Level 2 / Level 3
controls.purpose: Chooses an autonomy level for the current task. The choice can be changed until Submit is pressed. Disabled after submission.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Commits the chosen level as the single attempt for the current task. Enabled only after a level is chosen.

controls.label: Next Task / See Score
controls.purpose: Enabled after submission. Advances to the next task, and after task 8 shows the score summary.

controls.label: Start Over
controls.purpose: Shown on the summary screen; returns to task 1 with no level chosen.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Criteria-based judgment with one attempt per case and immediate explanatory feedback naming the rule that applied
keyQuestions: How much should the agent do on its own?
Does the result leave your control?
Can the result be checked quickly and objectively?
commonMisconceptions: A capable model deserves more autonomy on every task
Anything local is safe to run unattended
If a result is outward-bound, a quick look at it is enough
assessmentOpportunities: At least 7 of 8 levels correct on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Reading the task attributes is exploration and is not evidence
